original_cqs.expected_answer: The nucleation number density in the PP/PS blend interfacial region can increase five to six orders of magnitude compared to the other domains; specifically, the PP domain only reaches 3.25 x 10^6 cell/cm3, while the PS domain is about two orders of magnitude larger than the PP domain.

original_cqs.question: How does the foam morphology produced using Janus particles compare to that of the neat PPE/SAN blend?
original_cqs.expected_answer: The neat blend nearly did not foam and could not be properly evaluated, whereas the use of Janus particles produced homogenous foams characterized by small cell sizes (down to below 1 mm with 5 wt% JP) and relatively high densities (350–650 kg m-3).

original_cqs.question: According to Costeux et al., how does the cell size and nucleation density of foams produced from SAN blended with MMA-co-EA compare to those produced from the individual blend components?
original_cqs.expected_answer: Foams produced from the SAN/MMA-co-EA blends had more homogeneous cell size distribution and smaller cells (around 90–100 nm) with significantly higher cell nucleation densities (increased by several orders of magnitude) compared to foams obtained from either blend component alone.
